market_question: Israel x Hezbollah permanent peace deal by May 31, 2026?
reasoning: A permanent peace deal between Israel and Hezbollah is virtually impossible by May 2026. Hezbollah’s founding ideology rejects Israel’s existence, and Israel considers Hezbollah a terrorist proxy of Iran with no legitimate standing. No serious negotiations are underway, and any agreement would require fundamental concessions neither side will make. The 2.1% market probability is substantially above the true near-zero likelihood.
evidence_points: Hezbollah is ideologically committed to Israel’s destruction and will not sign a permanent peace deal.
Israel’s current government opposes any recognition of Hezbollah and continues military operations.
The 10‑day ceasefire example in the resolution criteria highlights how even temporary truces are fragile and short‑lived, underscoring the unlikelihood of a permanent accord.
sources_consulted: General knowledge of Israel‑Hezbollah conflict dynamics, recent escalations (2023‑2024), and political analysis.
